angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 21,712,797 km at 74.57 pc = 3.89 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 18925: the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax the radius was computed with (Table 1), 13.41 +/- 0.51 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b): 74.571 +/- 2.836 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 14.1252 +/- 0.7684 mas (same row, RUWE 10.84), 18.4 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 31.21 +/- 1.24 solar radii from Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 18925: radius 31.21 +1.24/-1.15 solar radii (Table 5), from the limb-darkened angular diameter 3.894 +/- 0.018 mas (NPOI, Table 4) and the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b): 21,712,797 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 3.64 +/- 0.25 solar masses from Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 18925: mass 3.64 +/- 0.25 solar masses (Table 6), from the PARAM Bayesian fit to PARSEC isochrones at the measured temperature; the paper calls its masses estimates only (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4589 +/- 58 K from Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 18925: effective temperature 4589 +/- 58 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 18925: effective temperature 4589 +/- 58 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/aa9d8b)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/gamma-persei.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 2.011, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Pulkovo spectrophotometric catalogue, table 5 (320-1080 nm, 2.5 nm steps, 10 nm resolution, absolute flux in W m^-2 m^-1)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
